description: Put tasks into the user's To-do backlog, the To-do widget on their canvas, in order and optionally under named steps. Use it when a conversation has settled what to do. Name the destination list in "list": call once without it to get the existing lists back on a LIST_NOT_FOUND answer, or pass create_list: true to make a new one. Always name a list, and file one plan into ONE list, its steps as "group". Write each text as a short title a person can say aloud (about 80 characters); the detail goes in "description". A rule, a trap or a decision is not something to do: file it with kind "note", so it stays as context and counts in no total. On a recent app your tasks wait in « To triage » until the human keeps them, and each gets a number (#42) shown by mnemosyne_todo_list. The app routes the write through the widget's own store, so what you file is what the user sees. Works with the app closed on a dev install (the headless daemon reads the file); an npm install has no daemon and needs the app running. To read the backlog back or change what is in it, see mnemosyne_todo_list, mnemosyne_todo_update and mnemosyne_todo_categories.

color.description: Hex colour (#rrggbb) for a list being created. Optional; the host picks the next swatch otherwise.

create_list.description: Create the list named in "list" when it does not exist. Default false, so an agent does not invent lists in someone's backlog without saying so.

list.description: Displayed name of the destination list, case-insensitive: "Today", "WIP", or a list the user created. Omitted, it goes to the first original list. An unknown name with create_list false is refused, and the answer gives the names that exist.

tasks.description: The tasks, in execution order. Each item is a string, or an object: "text" (a short title), "group" (the STEP it belongs to, e.g. "Step 1 · Mockup"; tasks with the same group are shown under one header), "description" (the detail, 4000 max), "kind" ("note" for context that is not a thing to do), "status" ("doing", "waiting" or "someday"), "priority" ("high" or "low"), "attachments" (absolute paths of files or folders the task is about, or {"path", "kind": "file"|"dir", "label"}). 300 characters max per text; a longer text is filed shortened and the answer says so.

name: mnemosyne_todo_add
